messages:
anya: Hi team — customer reports intermittent 401s from browser on Vercel edge functions. Happens only when using signed cookie auth (SameSite=None). They say node server SDK works, browser/edge fails on preflight sometimes. Repro attached below.

kevin: ugh, classic CORS+cookies dance. do we know which SDK version they're on?

anya: they're on @redwood/sdk-js 0.7.2 (edge build). Tried both fetch and the SDK wrapper.

sam: do they set credentials: 'include' on the browser fetch? and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials on the server?

anya: yes — they set credentials:'include' and server returns Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Browsers still send OPTIONS preflight and it sometimes returns 403 or 401. The 401 happens on the actual POST as well.

kevin: can you paste their minimal repro?

anya: here — simplified: \n```\n// browser\nfetch('https://api.prod.redwood.example/v1/generate', {\n  method: 'POST',\n  credentials: 'include',\n  headers: {\n    'Content-Type': 'application/json'\n  },\n  body: JSON.stringify({prompt: 'hi'})\n})\n```\nServer (Vercel Edge) returns set-cookie: __rwd_signed=...; SameSite=None; Secure; Path=/; HttpOnly

kevin: are they relying on the cookie being issued during the same flow that triggers the preflight? preflight (OPTIONS) doesn't include cookies, and some edge platforms block Set-Cookie on preflight responses.

sam: also note Vercel Edge functions have a different HTTP layer — they may not propagate cookies for OPTIONS in some setups. Have them check the edge function middleware that handles CORS.

anya: customer says behavior is intermittent: sometimes works for minutes, then starts 401s. Could be cached preflight or routing to legacy instance without the cookie store.

infra-bot: deploy 1938765600 completed to production (canary 10%).

kevin: that canary note matters — if canary doesn't have the auth shim, some requests will 401. ask them: do failures correlate with specific region or timestamp ranges?

anya: asked, they said errors spike around 09:05-09:12 UTC and mostly from EU users.

sam: possible: token signing keys rotated and canary uses old keyset. but they said only browser/edge clients affected. Could be SDK edge bundle sending Authorization header in preflight sometimes via a bug.

kevin: what does network tab show for failed preflight? response headers?

anya: one captured failed OPTIONS shows 403 and body "auth_required". No Set-Cookie on OPTIONS. The subsequent POST gets 401 "invalid_signed_cookie".

sam: OK repro steps to give customer: 1) upgrade @redwood/sdk-js to 0.8.1 — we fixed an edge bundling issue where the SDK sent an extra Authorization header in some edge runtimes. 2) ensure their Vercel middleware returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin exactly matching origin (no wildcard) and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true on both OPTIONS and POST. 3) don't set Set-Cookie on OPTIONS responses (move cookie issuance to the POST success) 4) check canary rollout: roll back or increase canary to 100% while debugging.

kevin: add: ask them to confirm cookie attributes: SameSite=None; Secure; Path=/; domain set to .example.com if they call subdomains. Browser won't send cookie if domain mismatch.

anya: sent upgrades and checklist. they replied they can't upgrade immediately. asked for a short mitigation.

sam: mitigation: server-side workaround is to accept a short-lived bearer token passed in query param for edge callers (not ideal security-wise) or accept Authorization header from edge SDK only when origin matches. But easier: add an allowlist on server that treats missing cookie + valid origin as session if there's a fallback header.

kevin: also there is a temporary fix client-side: set mode: 'cors' and credentials:'include' and ensure you don't call the API from service worker scope that captures OPTIONS differently. Some frameworks (Next/Vercel) register service workers that interfere.

anya: customer tried disabling service worker with no luck.

sam: last thing — request they capture full HAR of failing flow and include request/response headers for OPTIONS and POST. that will show where cookie gets dropped.

kevin: i'll check canary keyset and edge auth shim logs for 09:05-09:12 UTC EU. if we find mismatch we can hotfix.

anya: thanks — passing to infra. will update thread with HAR. :thumbsup:
